sections.h2: Where does a Pitt County deed get recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for Pitt County land is recorded at the Pitt County Register of Deeds, at 100 E. 1st Street in Greenville. Weekday hours on the county page are 8:00 to 5:00, and the phone is 252-902-1650.

The same office keeps deeds, deeds of trust, easements, plats and the other land papers that make up the chain of title. Some of the records go back to the 1700s, since Pitt County was formed in 1760. For a seller, the office matters at one moment above all: the deed that moves the house to a buyer has to land in these books before it protects anyone.

sections.h2: Does the order of filing matter for a Pitt County sale?
sections.html:
Because the first paper on file wins. According to the state recording statute, an unfiled deed or option has no force against creditors with liens or buyers who paid value, and ranking among claims follows filing time.

Greenville is where that time stamp gets set, which is why every closing ends with a filing step. A signed deed left in a drawer protects nobody. Hold an old deed from a family transfer that never reached the office? File it, or talk to an attorney, before you advertise the house.

sections.h2: What will Pitt County charge to file a deed?
sections.html:
The General Assembly sets the fees, and the county page says they match in every county. The Pitt summary lists these items:

  • A general instrument such as a deed or easement starts at $26 and adds $4 per page after page 15.
  • A plat costs $21 per sheet, and a non-standard document adds $25.
  • A certified copy costs $5 for page one plus $2 per extra page.
  • Releasing a mortgage costs nothing.

The county's summary lists mortgages and deeds of trust at $56 for the first 15 pages, while the statute text, G.S. 161-10, prints $64 with a 35-page allowance. Call before sending a lender document so the check matches. Cash, check, money order and card payments are accepted.

sections.h2: How is the Pitt County deed stamp tax figured?
sections.html:
The excise tax runs a dollar for every $500 of price, with a leftover part of $500 counting as a full one. Pitt's records page says it follows the sale price.

The seller carries the duty, according to the excise tax statute, and it has to be paid before the register will accept the deed. Pitt keeps half the money and the State receives the other half. Look for the line on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: Does Pitt County accept electronic filing?
sections.html:
Yes. The county takes electronic filings through several vendors and tells filers to call each one to compare prices. Four vendors are listed, each with its own phone number on the county FAQ.

Most sellers never touch this step, since the closing office sends the deed and the buyer's loan papers together. A family transfer with no lender is different: ask whoever prepared the deed whether they file electronically or in person, and who covers the vendor charge.

sections.h2: How can a Pitt County owner watch for deed fraud and check records?
sections.html:
Pitt County has an alert sign-up that notifies owners whenever a filing matches their name or property. The county also runs an online search for recorded documents from September 1762 to the present, searchable by grantor, grantee, document type, book and page, or date range.

  • Search the grantor index for your name to see every recorded deed or lien tied to you.
  • Use book and page numbers from an old deed to pull the full document.
  • Use the county's Online Parcel Information System, run by Tax Administration and GIS, to view parcel boundaries, assessed values, tax districts and flood zones.
  • Older index books can be used on site at the Greenville office.

Do this before listing, especially with an inherited house. A loan that was never released, or a missing link in the ownership record, takes less effort to fix while no buyer is waiting.

sections.h2: What other papers might a Pitt County sale involve?
sections.html:
A Pitt County closing, apart from the deed, can include a deed of trust for the buyer's loan, a recorded release of the seller's old loan, and sometimes a plat or easement. Each one is filed separately and priced under the fee list above.

  • Old loan: confirm the lender recorded a satisfaction.
  • New loan: the buyer's lender records its own deed of trust.
  • Seller financing: see the contract for deed rules in Chapter 47H, which call for recording within five business days.

The county's FAQ lists agreements, assignments, assumed names, leases and subdivision maps among the land-related documents the office records.

sections.h2: What else does the Pitt County register's office keep?
sections.html:
The office is more than a deed counter. It holds birth and death certificates for events in the county, issues marriage licenses, files notary commissions and gives the oath to every notary public. Veterans can file military discharge records here, and the county waives the charge for filing or copying them.

It also takes Uniform Commercial Code financing statements on personal property, listed at $38 for one or two pages. The overlap that helps sellers is notary service. The county lists a $10 notarial act fee tied to a filing, so someone who has not yet signed a deed can ask about doing it at the counter. Call 252-902-1650 first, and bring photo identification.

sections.h2: What does Pitt County's history mean for old deeds?
sections.html:
Pitt County was formed in 1760, and the county says its oldest records include land grants, indentures and property agreements from the 1700s. Online search reaches back to September 1762, and index books for older records are kept on site: look up the grantor or grantee in the alphabetical index, note the book and page, then pull the full document with that reference.

For a seller, an old farm or family tract can have a chain of deeds that runs back generations. If a deed in that chain was never filed, or a name is spelled differently from one deed to the next, a buyer's title search will flag it. Start the search early, and keep every book and page number you find.

sections.h2: What should a Pitt County seller do before closing?
sections.html:
Begin with a title check. Pull the deed that put the house in your name, confirm each old loan has a filed release, and ask the tax office what is owed.

Property tax lives in a different office. According to the collection statute, each bill falls due on September 1, and interest begins after January 5. Pitt County Tax Administration, not this page, gives the balance on your parcel.

Repairs, tenants and estate delays do not block a quick sale to a direct cash buyer. The filing steps stay the same: the deed goes to Greenville.

faqs.q: Where is the Pitt County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: At 100 E. 1st Street, Greenville, NC 27834. Weekdays only, 8:00 to 5:00, and the county lists 252-902-1650 for questions.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamp tax in a Pitt County sale?
faqs.a: Sellers do. The statute names the transferor, and the office takes the payment at the counter. Your settlement statement should show the line.

faqs.q: Is there a charge to file a mortgage release in Pitt County?
faqs.a: No. The county lists satisfactions and cancellations as free. The lender is the one that files the release, so ask yours to do it.

faqs.q: Is there an online deed search for Pitt County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says documents recorded from September 1762 forward can be searched online by name, type, book and page, or dates.

faqs.q: What is the base fee for a Pitt County deed?
faqs.a: $26 buys a general instrument of up to 15 pages, then each extra page adds $4. Plats are $21 a sheet. Get the final total for your own document by phone, extras included.
